question.problem:
Find the second-degree Taylor polynomial ${P}_{2}(x)$ of $f(x)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)$ about $x=\frac{\pi }{3}.$

${P}_{2}(x)=$
{{field-1}}$\,+$
{{field-2}}$(x-\frac{\pi }{3})\,-$
{{field-3}}${(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2}$
question.worked_solution:
To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=\frac{\pi }{3},$ we plug $a=\frac{\pi }{3}$ into the general formula to give

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(\frac{\pi }{3})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})(x-\frac{\pi }{3})+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3}){(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2}.
$$

So, we need to work out $f(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ and ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & f(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\sqrt{3} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =1 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ and ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3})$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =\sqrt{3}+1(x-\frac{\pi }{3})+(-\sqrt{3})\cdot \frac{1}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2} \\  & =\sqrt{3}+1(x-\frac{\pi }{3})-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
